title: Crates re-organization
description:
# Crates re-organization

## Provenance

Created with explicit user authorization after fetching main and searching registered worktrees and local Artagon Beads records did not recover the earlier epic. This is a new tracker record for the documented target, not a recovered historical epic.

## Goal

Re-organize the existing single library into a flat crates/frost-* layout with a frost-api facade whose Rust import remains frost. Establish a reviewed acyclic dependency graph around actual semantic and execution responsibilities. Preserve the public API contracts, fixed freeze/thaw partners, no_std/core/alloc/std support, additive features, and Rust 1.99.1 edition 2024.

## Scope and sequence

1. Approve crate boundaries, names, facade feature forwarding, internal visibility, dependency graph, and migration mapping from existing modules. Update the current single-package policy in the same migration change.
2. Move implementation, unit/integration/doc tests, examples, benchmarks, factories, and metadata to their owning crates without weakening tests or duplicating production algorithms.
3. Keep optional fuzz, Loom, Kani and other verification harnesses isolated from consumers, colocated with their owning crate according to CRATES.md; preserve production linkage and package exclusions.
4. Update root Make/CI orchestration, package tests, isolated feature/embedded matrices, source paths and documentation links. Verify facade API/feature parity and no accidental dependency leakage.
5. Record crate-specific verification and benchmark evidence plus source-to-migration mapping. Publish no crates as part of the layout migration.

## Acceptance

- Every current module and harness has an explicit owner and migration path.
- Existing consumer import spelling and intended public contracts are preserved, with reviewed explicit compatibility decisions for unavoidable changes.
- Crate-local layout, metadata, scenario factories and verification standards satisfy the separate standards epic frost-wou.
- Core-only, alloc-only, std, individual integrations, downstream codecs, embedded atomic/non-atomic builds, package extraction tests and relevant Miri/model gates are verified against the migrated source.
- No empty placeholder library packages or unsupported performance/proof claims.

## Relationship

The standards and testing epic frost-wou supplies the structure and verification rules and is a prerequisite for completing this migration. The present standards implementation does not perform package moves or mark this re-organization complete.

title: Approve package boundaries and migration mapping
description:
Produce the package list, single responsibility per package, complete module/test/benchmark/example/harness mapping, acyclic normal-dependency graph, seal/coherence plan, facade feature map, and compatibility notes required by docs/design/crate-layout.md. Resolve inherent-method and foreign-trait ownership before any move.

Acceptance: a reviewed design preserves public frost paths, additive features, no_std/core/alloc/std support, fixed freeze/thaw partners, Rust 1.99.1 edition 2024, and the production linkage of private harnesses. Do not create placeholder packages. Standards epic frost-wou is the prerequisite.

title: Move crate code and consumers under approved boundaries
description:
Implement the approved flat crates/frost-* mapping. Move production modules, contract/unit/doc tests, benchmarks, examples, and factory/catalog ownership without weakening behavior or duplicating algorithms. Update the current one-package policy in AGENTS.md, CRATES.md and design decisions in the same change as the first move.

Acceptance: stable catalog IDs survive moves; public import spelling stays frost; representative identity, ownership, iterator, integer storage and snapshot contracts remain intact. No policy-only interval authorizes an unreviewed split.

title: Colocate isolated fuzz and verification packages
description:
Move each owned fuzz package to its package-local fuzz directory and Loom, Kani and downstream-consumer packages to verification subdirectories. Use workspace exclusion or explicit isolated workspaces and keep independent lockfiles.

Acceptance: private-source harness paths compile against the actual relocated production files; normal library and core-only dependency graphs contain no proof, model or fuzz tools; no duplicate harness locations remain. Preserve documented bounds, assumptions and limitations.

title: Validate facade API and feature parity after the split
description:
Implement and check frost-api facade reexports and feature forwarding using the approved feature map. Keep the Rust library import frost.

Acceptance: every current public path and compile-fail doctest still resolves as intended; fixed partners, bounds, hasher choices, and auto-trait contracts survive; each isolated feature plus core/alloc/std and integer atomic/non-atomic embedded builds pass. Document any deliberately reviewed compatibility change rather than silently weakening tests.

title: Migrate Make, CI and package verification to the workspace
description:
Update Make recipes, CI, packaging and documentation for the approved workspace. Discover packages and relevant targets from cargo metadata with jq in recipes. Preserve Bash 3.2 and GNU Make 3.81 compatibility.

Acceptance: help and dry runs remain observational; failures propagate; every intended member and isolated package is exercised; extracted package builds, optional feature and embedded matrices remain isolated; shell-check passes on the minimum available Bash.

title: Record verification evidence for the migrated source
description:
After the crate, harness, facade and orchestration migrations converge, run the complete applicable matrix and record new evidence against the migrated source revision.

Acceptance: make check/verify, feature and embedded gates and required ownership/model checks have actual receipts with versions, bounds and limitations; relevant benchmarks retain comparable native controls and raw observations; coverage is remeasured with unchanged or explicitly reviewed denominators. Historical pre-migration results are not reused as proof for moved code. Resolve review findings before closing the reorganization epic.

title: Crate structure, verification, and benchmark standards
description:
# Crate structure, verification, and benchmark standards

## Goal

Define and implement repository standards in CRATES.md for the crate re-organization: src, tests, benches, fuzzing, Loom, Rust-based formal verification, property tests, mutation testing, high public-API coverage, test/benchmark metadata and tags, and deterministic parameterized benchmark data factories.

This is a separate epic linked to crates re-organization epic frost-wlt. That migration depends on this standards epic. frost-wlt was created with explicit user authorization after the earlier epic could not be recovered; it is not presented as a recovered historical record. Package moves belong to frost-wlt, not this epic.

## Scope

- Use write-enabled NTM Opus, Fable, and Argon lanes with economical research subagents and current primary-source documentation.
- Establish a canonical crate directory and ownership standard in CRATES.md, update the repository guidance and design/maintenance entry points.
- Define risk-based API coverage, semantic obligations, feature/target matrices, mandatory gates, tool scopes, and explicit exceptions. Never report desired coverage as measured coverage.
- Add structured stable metadata/tags for tests and benchmarks, discoverability and validation, and parameterized reproducible workload factories with exact scenario guarantees and native controls.
- Specify and demonstrate Rust-based fuzz, property, mutation, Loom, Miri, and bounded/formal verification integration without adding these to normal runtime dependencies.
- Use NTM Terra to implement GitHub issue forms and PR templates aligned with the repository's evidence and verification requirements.

## Acceptance

- CRATES.md is the canonical linked standard, with target layout and current implementation state clearly distinguished.
- Test strategy covers public APIs, semantic laws, panic/ownership paths, feature combinations, portability, concurrency, and adversarial inputs; tags, manifests, reproducibility, and coverage/mutation accounting are concrete and checkable.
- Parameterized factory support has deterministic seeds, bounded generation, exact requested shapes or explicit rejection, correctness oracles, and replayable benchmark identifiers.
- Templates are valid and provide focused bug, feature/design, research, and PR information without secrets or unnecessary blanket checklists.
- Epic tasks, dependencies, and acceptance criteria reflect the final reviewed proposal and implementation; the re-organization relationship is recorded once its real ID is known.
- Relevant focused checks, make check, and any affected shell/feature/embedded gates pass, or actual blockers and remaining gates are explicitly recorded.

## Baseline

Repository commit 6ab0918dbbf655894d8d3176b81091bd28899c5f; Rust 1.99.1 edition 2024; one current library package with optional isolated verification packages. All four NTM lanes must preserve library semantic contracts and unrelated changes.
notes:
Reviewed plan: CRATES.md governs the current single package and the future flat crates/frost-* layout. Initial implementation is frost-wou.1 through frost-wou.5. Adoption follow-ups are frost-wou.6 (full API obligation curation), .7 (branch/profile and CI baselines), .8 (mutation baseline), .9 (high structural coverage targets), and .10 (automated dependency-isolation guards). The epic remains open until its adoption gates are satisfied; package moves remain in linked frost-wlt.
Implementation tasks frost-wou.1 through frost-wou.5 are complete with checked acceptance criteria. Evidence: verification/crate-standards-validation/README.md and after-coverage.json. Standards epic stays open for adoption tasks frost-wou.6 through frost-wou.10; reorganization epic frost-wlt remains dependent and its migration tasks remain open. No migration, commit, push, or GitHub workflow execution is claimed.

Branches and semantic API obligation coverage are unmeasured. Durable sanitized observation: verification/crate-standards-validation/baseline-coverage.json. Coverage gap work is frost-wou.5. Target thresholds must remain distinct from this baseline.

title: Automate verification dependency isolation checks
description:
# Automate verification dependency isolation checks

Turn the current isolated-package and cargo-tree evidence into a required dependency-leakage guard for the future workspace. Keep metadata parsing in Make recipes with jq.

Acceptance:
- Check normal dependency graphs for core-only, alloc-only and supported optional profiles.
- Reject accidental library dependencies on test, fuzz, model, proof or catalog tooling.
- Check each isolated harness remains independently buildable with its own lockfile and production linkage.
- Include negative fixtures for the guard without mutating the real library manifest during checks.

title: Implement tagged verification catalog and workload factories
description: Implement typed deterministic parameterized benchmark/test data factories, regression tests, test and benchmark metadata with stable IDs and tags, and validation/discovery tooling; preserve runtime dependencies.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Catalog validates stable metadata, controlled tags, source/target discovery and measured benchmark-case registration; negative fixtures reject drift. Legacy uncurated semantics remain explicit.
- [x] Deterministic factories reject invalid or oversized parameters before generation, preserve exact shapes and u64 boundary behavior, and drive real benchmarks with correctness oracles outside timing.
notes: Fable completed deterministic factories, boundary/preflight fixes, 12 factory regressions and 914 exact benchmark records. Remaining discovery/schema and portable inventory work transferred to Terra after Fable reported partial completion and became idle; root records the lease handoff in the round3 ledger.

title: Curate the complete public API obligation inventory
description:
# Curate the complete public API obligation inventory

Apply CRATES.md to every public item under the supported feature profiles. Distinguish discovered test/benchmark records from reviewed semantic evidence. Replace legacy scaffolded records with reviewed contracts, oracles, tags and source provenance; do not infer semantic coverage from test counts or textual symbol matches.

Acceptance:
- Inventory public API obligations by operation, ownership, representative, iterator, feature and concurrency contract, including uncovered obligations.
- Link each covered obligation to an asserting case and identify its actual feature/target scope.
- Preserve stable metadata IDs and record curated/scaffolded/uncovered counts explicitly.
- Run the isolated catalog validator and relevant tests; never weaken discovery to hide missing records.

This is standards adoption after the initial catalog infrastructure, not evidence that current semantic coverage is complete.

title: Measure branch and isolated-profile coverage
description:
# Measure branch and isolated-profile coverage

Record the first supported branch measurement and coverage for core-only, alloc-only and important isolated features. Match compiler, target, feature profile and denominator when comparing baselines. Establish a Linux CI baseline separately from the measured aarch64-apple-darwin baseline.

Acceptance:
- Preserve raw summaries, tool versions, commands, exclusions, covered/total counts and source identity.
- Keep unmeasured metrics explicit; no zero-denominator percentage claim.
- Establish scoped non-regression baselines independently of portable adoption floors.
- Set branch and profile targets only after reviewing actual measurements and justified exclusions.

title: Establish mutation baseline and triage survivors
description:
# Establish mutation baseline and triage survivors

Run the pinned mutation tool against priority public API algorithms using the configured deterministic tests. The initial implementation validates missing-tool failure, not a mutation score.

Acceptance:
- Record tool/compiler versions, source identity, selected files, test command and raw outcome artifacts.
- Triage every survivor, timeout and unviable mutant; add regression tests for genuine gaps.
- Equivalent-mutant and other waivers include the rationale and owner/review information required by CRATES.md.
- Report the precise score denominator and excluded outcomes; adopt a gate only after a reviewed baseline.

title: Reach high coverage targets with meaningful API tests
description:
# Reach the high coverage targets with meaningful API tests

Expand assertions in the low-coverage mutable family and native capability modules identified by the baseline. The initial six API regression tests improve specific obligations; they do not establish complete coverage.

Acceptance:
- Reach the proposed 90% source lines, 90% regions and 85% functions within explicitly matched measurement scopes, or document narrowly reviewed exceptions.
- Prioritize independent standard-library differential tests, bounded operation traces, representative retention, partial iteration and ownership/drop behavior.
- Link assertions to the curated API obligation inventory; do not add tests solely to execute lines or weaken production behavior.
- Raise adoption gates using reviewed evidence and preserve raw before/after results.
